questions.knowledge_point: Projecting a Vector Onto a Perpendicular Vector
questions.problem: Let $a=5i-4j+3k$ and $b=-7i+xj+k.$ Given that the scalar projection of $a$ onto $b$ is zero, find the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =5\cdot (-7)+(-4)\cdot x+3\cdot 1 \\  & =-4x-32.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ -4x-32 & =0 \\ 4x & =-32 \\ x & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $c=⟨-3,\sqrt{3},1⟩$ and $d=⟨x,0,-12⟩.$ Given that the scalar projection of $c$ onto $d$ is zero, find the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $c$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $d$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
c⊥d\,⟹\,c\cdot d=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot d & ={c}_{x}\cdot {d}_{x}+{c}_{y}\cdot {d}_{y}+{c}_{z}\cdot {d}_{z} \\  & =(-3)\cdot x+\sqrt{3}\cdot 0+1\cdot (-12) \\  & =-3x-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot d & =0 \\ -3x-12 & =0 \\ 3x & =-12 \\ x & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Scalar Projection Using Components
questions.worked_solution:
Using the scalar projection formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{s}\,r & =\frac{r\cdot s}{|\,s\,|} \\  & =\frac{{r}_{x}{s}_{x}+{r}_{y}{s}_{y}+{r}_{z}{s}_{z}}{\sqrt{{s}_{x}^{2}+{s}_{y}^{2}+{s}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{(-1)(2)+(2)(0)+(3)(0)}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-2}{\sqrt{4}} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Projecting a Vector Onto a Perpendicular Vector
questions.worked_solution:
Since $p$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $q$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
p⊥q\,⟹\,p\cdot q=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y}+{p}_{z}\cdot {q}_{z} \\  & =3\cdot x+(-1)\cdot 1+2\cdot 1 \\  & =3x+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ 3x+1 & =0 \\ 3x & =-1 \\ x & =-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
